details.releaseNotesExcerpt: <details open> tests : make MoE router selection independent of the backend noise (#30818) * tests : make MoE router selection independent of the backend noise The router scores are in the range [0, 1), so a random draw can leave the last expert (or expert group) still selected and the first one dropped tied within the noise between the backends. They then route a token to different experts and the logits differ by 4e-3 instead of the usual 5e-7. Beam is the only arch here with a real top-k (8 experts, 2 used) and a group top-k (4 groups, 2 used), so it is the only one that hits this: 2 of 20 seeds failed on an M2 Ultra, the other MoE archs select 2 of 2 and cannot tie. Fill the selection bias with a ramp of step 2 to give every expert a score range of its own, which turns the top-k into a function of the expert index alone. details.releaseNotesExcerpt: <details open> ggml-cpu : select the NEON fp32->fp16 conversion (#30505) The __ARM_NEON branch defines both GGML_CPU_COMPUTE_* macros but selects only FP16_TO_FP32, so FP32_TO_FP16 falls through to the portable software conversion while neon_compute_fp32_to_fp16, a single fcvt, stays defined and referenced by nothing. __POWER9_VECTOR__ and __riscv_zfhmin select both. Add an #error pair that refuses a branch defining a COMPUTE macro without selecting it. That is how this stayed unnoticed: the fallback silently supplies a correct software implementation, so the only symptom is a hardware instruction nothing ever reaches. The FP16_TO_FP32 half carries a !defined(__F16C__) carve-out, because PR 30343 keeps that direction on the lookup table on purpose. Replace the comment above the fallback: it singled out NEON and POWER9 and pointed at a selection that now happens in the branch itself. </details> **Website:** - <https://llama.app> **Attestations:** - <https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp
